text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland, after a total of 10 years in office, announced she would resign to give her Labour Party a fresh start for next year's election. Labour Party leader Torbjoern Jagland will succeed her as prime minister on Friday and promises to keep policies unchanged.
- Didrik Schnitler, president in the Industry Federation, says Brundtland has been an impressive prime minister.
- Special U.N. envoy Terje Roed Larsen could join Jagland's new goverment.

- Gro Harlem Brundtlands announcment did not seem to influence the markets. Head economist Harald Magnus Andreassen in brokerfirm Elcon Securities does not expect any change to the government's policy when Jagland take over as prime minister.

- Industry and Energy Minister Jens Stoltenberg could switch to the job as finance minister in the new government. If so, finance minister Sigbjoern Johnsen might become parliamentary leader for the ruling Labour Party.

- Airlines Scandinavian Airlines System and Braathens SAFE are fighting over passengers on flights between Oslo and Stockholm. Two weeks before Braathens starts their flights to Stockholm, SAS has reduced the price of a Euro-ticket by 14 percent.
